query: Explain the difference between `git merge` and `git rebase` in two short paragraphs, with one sentence on when to prefer each.
result:
Both commands combine the work from one branch into another, but they differ in how they record history. `git merge` joins two lines of history with a new merge commit that has two parents, so the existing commits stay exactly as they were and the branch structure is preserved. `git rebase` instead lifts your commits off their original base and replays them one by one on top of a new base, rewriting them with new hashes so the history reads as one straight line. Merge is non-destructive but can leave a tangle of merge commits; rebase gives a cleaner history but changes commits, so it should not be used on commits others have already pulled.

Prefer `git merge` when a branch is shared or already published, or when you want an accurate record of when work was integrated. Prefer `git rebase` when you are cleaning up your own local feature branch before opening a pull request, so it lands as a tidy, linear sequence of commits.
